RockSigma provides its proprietary software solution named BEMIS (including BEMIS 1.0 and BEMIS 2.0) built on over 10 to 12 years of applied rock mechanics research conducted alongside Swedish mining house LKAB and Luleå University of Technology.
The BEMIS 2.0 architecture features self-calibrating algorithms designed to estimate source parameters and hypocentre locations without needing expensive physical reference blasts.
The algorithms include an integrated self-service tomographic imaging solution to map velocity variations and assess structural rock mass stability within underground mines.
RockSigma's primary product is the BEMIS Compute Engine, developed as a highly scalable, fully automated software environment built to run on modern data architectures.

According to company specifications, the software operates with a fully automated workflow that handles large seismic volumes with zero manual intervention required, actively scaling to the operational activity levels of any size mine.
The company delivers its high-performance seismic capabilities via a flexible, cloud-ready Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) subscription model.
RockSigma is a software provider focused on mine-site installations and custom deployments rather than maintaining a traditional speculative multi-client seismic data library.
Its data strategy centers on an open ecosystem, sensor-neutral data platform that ingests custom client arrays and aggregates data across multi-vendor equipment types.
RockSigma's solutions have been applied and validated directly across client-owned production datasets at more than a dozen mines globally across five continents.
The BEMIS software system delivers real-time monitoring tools that output instantaneous event localization and automated characterization to reduce post-event operational waiting periods.

RockSigma introduces time-lapse/4D predictive elements via its seismic activity level forecasting tool, allowing mine operators to track how the rock mass changes and responds dynamically to production over time.
The BEMIS 2.0 package incorporates advanced integration for Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) systems to continuously process massive streams of fiber-optic acoustic data at mine-scale.

RockSigma embeds artificial intelligence and advanced statistical algorithms directly into its core BEMIS system to achieve automated, high-precision processing reaching beyond manual human analysis speeds.
The platform relies on industrial AI and self-learning statistical models that automatically adapt and auto-calibrate to changing underground topologies and wave propagation variances.

RockSigma offers a seamless software extension to the widely adopted geotechnical analysis software package mXrap, automating the transfer of AI-interpreted seismic source parameters and data catalogs into downstream rock engineering workflows.

RockSigma operates exclusively within deep mining and microseismic environments, rather than traditional large-scale oil and gas sectors. Its foundational mathematical algorithms and automatic processing software, BEMIS, were developed in close, multi-year collaboration with LKAB (Luossavaara-Kiirunavaara AB) for its massive underground iron ore mines in Kiruna and Malmberget, Sweden.
As stated by the company's leadership, RockSigma's live, automated seismic processing systems are actively deployed across four of the world's largest caving mines globally.

No traditional named oil and gas commercial exploration contracts are documented, as the product is purpose-built to locate induced micro-seismicity from industrial applications (like mining and deep geothermal systems) rather than large-scale oil reservoir imaging.

Rather than running heavy local hardware arrays or regional data warehouses, RockSigma delivers its flagship BEMIS Compute Engine via a flexible SaaS-offering (Software as a Service) and remote expert services managed from its headquarters in Luleå, Sweden.

Despite operating centrally out of Sweden, the cloud-delivered software has successfully processed data and executed validation test deployments at more than a dozen mines and multiple energy projects on five continents.
According to disclosures from company executives, RockSigma achieved a 30% increase in total revenue year-over-year following a transition from research and development into a sales-driven structure.
Driven by this shift towards commercialization, the company recorded a rapid 500% increase in export sales volume over the same twelve-month operating period.
Tracxn venture capital database records document early financial capitalization, including a $144K seed funding round backed by Swedish investment firm Northern Capsek Ventures.

RockSigma has built a technical product alliance with the specialized mining software package mXrap, ensuring BEMIS directly integrates and extends into mXrap applications to support daily geotechnical and mine design workflows.

The company won the Swedish Mining Innovation Award 2024 for its advanced processing project targeting Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) systems in mines, collaborating extensively with industrial research networks to deploy sensor-neutral software architectures.

While its share in the vast global oil and gas seismic imaging market is negligible, RockSigma holds a distinct, highly niche footprint in deep underground caving operations, with validation across more than ten production mines globally by the end of 2023.
The company's processing framework is uniquely integrated into the core operations of LKAB, which runs some of the largest, most seismically active underground iron ore extraction networks on Earth.

Survey Engine® Seismic+ includes enhanced processing functionality in the frequency domain with histograms and a full suite of varying filters, such as Time Varying Filtering, Swell Filter, Heave Filter, and Trace Mixing/Stacking.
Survey Engine® Seismic+ features increased depth accuracy through the implementation of Multiple Sound Velocity Profiles based on specific feature types within the sub-seabed.
The Survey Engine® Software Suite boasts an unlimited project size capacity and a 20GB single file upload limit alongside batch processing capability.

Version 10.1 of Survey Engine® integrates major structural updates focused on data management that allow the application to handle massive datasets effortlessly, utilizing user-selectable channel sub-sets.

Coda Octopus Products Ltd. functions strictly as a technology vendor providing hardware like the DA4G Acquisition Systems and software suites, meaning it does not own or license a commercial multi-client data library.
To handle external project data, the Survey Engine® Software Suite integrates support for the industry-standard Seabed Survey Data Model (SSDM).
The DA4G Series of Acquisition Systems delivers purpose-built, real-time data acquisition from sub-bottom profiler sensors, supporting simultaneous real-time recording of both raw and processed data.
Coda Octopus utilizes the 4G USE® Multi-Sensor Platform for real-time 3D data acquisition, visualization, and live multi-user data sharing across a shared project database.

The Survey Engine® Automatic Object Detection Package (SEADP) employs artificial intelligence algorithms to automate the detection, positioning, and sizing (length, width, height) of subsea anomalies.
The Survey Engine® Seabed Classification Module uses AI-based methodology to automatically recognize and segment up to six distinct seabed composition types from sonar data.

Viridien's Geovation software serves as its benchmark seismic processing system, featuring over 45 years of geophysical software evolution and including more than 300 batch processing modules.
The company utilizes advanced Elastic Full-Waveform Inversion (FWI) algorithms that bypass conventional migration steps to output subsurface reflectivity images directly.
Viridien collaborates with NVIDIA to optimize its proprietary seismic imaging algorithms using accelerated computing platforms.
Viridien operates a global high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure delivering over 700 petaflops of compute capacity globally.

Petroleum Development Oman (PDO) awarded Viridien a three-year contract in January 2025 to provide advanced land seismic imaging services at its dedicated processing center in Muscat, Oman.

Groupement Hassi Bir Rekaiz (a Sonatrach and PTTEP joint operatorship) awarded Viridien a 13-month contract in April 2025 to reimage two legacy 3D seismic datasets covering 2,400 sq km in the Berkine Basin, Eastern Algeria.
Aker BP secured a long-term agreement with Viridien in mid-2026 for advanced ocean bottom node (OBN) processing capabilities on the Norwegian Continental Shelf.
Viridien operates its largest Dedicated Processing Center (DPC) worldwide in Muscat, Oman, alongside fully operational advanced High-Performance Computing (HPC) imaging hubs in Abu Dhabi and the UK.
The company expanded its total proprietary cloud and infrastructure computing capacity to 690 petaflops as of June 2026.
Viridien supports global subsurface data processing through specialized geoscience hubs located in strategic industry locations including Singapore and Houston.
For the full year 2025, Viridien reported total segment revenue of $1,165 million (up 4% year-on-year), with its core Geoscience division increasing 10% to $444 million.
Due to project delays and geopolitical conflict in the Middle East, Q2 2026 segment revenue dropped 15% year-over-year to $232 million.
Despite near-term revenue pressure, the company's Geoscience backlog reached $306 million at the end of June 2026, marking a 19% increase compared to December 2025.

Viridien entered a multi-year partnership with NVIDIA in February 2026 to optimize its proprietary seismic imaging algorithms using NVIDIA’s advanced HPC platforms, tensor cores, and mixed-precision computing.

In March 2026, Viridien partnered with BGP and the Ministry of Natural Resources of Guyana to execute a massive multi-client 3D seismic acquisition and imaging program spanning 25,000 square kilometers.
Viridien launched an 18-month multi-client Integrated Prospectivity and Subsurface Study in September 2026 in collaboration with PETRONAS through Malaysia Petroleum Management.

Viridien commands a top-tier market share via its proprietary powerhouse software system, Geovation, which incorporates over 45 years of geophysical software evolution for advanced subsurface imaging.

The company maintains deep operating integration with Supermajors and National Oil Companies, illustrated by a transformational multi-year partnership signed in 2026 with a major international oil company to externalize their in-house seismic processing worldwide.

The company's unique high-margin structure is sustained by its asset-light business model, delivering a robust 59% adjusted EBITDA margin within its Data, Digital & Energy Transition segment during the first half of 2026.
